statement: Explain what banking means in law, the sources of banking regulation, and why provisions apply differently to different banks
source_caveats: This unit states statutory provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 as summarised by the courseware at its date. No primary text (the Acts as amended to the 30 June 2026 cut-off, including the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act of 2025) was retrieved in this batch, so every section number and rule is taught only as the courseware states it and may have changed; the batch must be re-checked against the consolidated Acts before publication.

The courseware says the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 "came into force from 6th March 1934"; that date is the date of enactment as commonly stated, and the Act commenced on 1 April 1935. The commencement date is therefore not taught; only the purpose of the Act is taught.

The courseware states that the Banking Regulation Act 1949 was applicable to Jammu and Kashmir from 1956; the courseware text about the Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020 (effective 26 June 2020, primary and state co-operative banks) and the 2019 non-banking finance company amendments (net owned fund limit of Rs 100 crore and different amounts notified for categories, powers to supersede the board, remove or debar auditors, frame schemes of amalgamation) is dated and not checked; taught only at the level of principle.

The courseware reference to Section 5(b) as the definition of banking, Section 22 as the licence, Section 6(1) as permitted business, Section 8 as prohibited trading, Section 9 as disposal of non-banking assets within seven years, Section 49A as deposits withdrawable by cheque and the sections on government powers (Sections 7(1), 10B, 36AA, 22, 14A, 4, 53, 52, 45Y, 19, 29, 35, 38A) were not checked against the Act; they are used only as the courseware cites them.
Numbers in the numerical items are invented and checked in tests/content/batch-brbl-a-u01-b001.test.ts (a small test of counts and structure, since the unit has no calculations).
The courseware check-your-progress questions were not copied; questions are independently written.

statement: Explain the licensing of banking companies under Section 22: the discretion of the Reserve Bank and the conditions it must be satisfied about
source_caveats: The unit is the courseware account of Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provisions (Sections 10, 10A, 10B, 10BB, 10C, 11, 12, 12B, 13, 15, 17, 19, 22, 23, 29A, 35, 36AA, 36AB, 36ACA) and of RBI guidelines on licensing and governance. No Act text and no RBI direction was retrieved, so every section number and limit is taught only as the courseware states it and must be checked against the consolidated Act as at 30 June 2026 (the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 amended several of these sections) before publication.

Held back as not verified or superseded: the rupee amounts of minimum paid-up capital and reserves in Section 11 (the courseware quotes the old statutory scale, Rs 15 lakh, Rs 20 lakh, Rs 10 lakh, Rs 5 lakh and so on), the dividend declaration conditions (capital adequacy and net NPA tests, 40 per cent payout) which later RBI directions replaced, the 2013 on-tap universal and small finance bank guideline details, the April 2021 and April 2022 RBI circulars on the Chair, committees, age and tenure of directors and the 15-year, 12-year and 70-year limits for managing directors and chief executives, and the foreign shareholding and strategic investment thresholds of 2004 and 2005. No question asks these figures.

The courseware sentence on the temporary prohibition on directors of Section 25 / Section 8 companies managing a bank is ambiguous (three months and a further nine months); it is not taught as a number.
The courseware describes substantial interest as exceeding Rs 5 lakh or ten per cent of paid-up capital without saying which applies; no calculation uses it.

The Banking Regulation Act as amended in 2025 changed the tenure of directors other than the chairman and whole-time director and the definition of substantial interest; the courseware figure of eight years is taught only as the courseware states it and is flagged as likely to have changed.
The courseware check-your-progress answers were not copied; questions are independently written.
Numbers in the numerical items are invented and checked in tests/content/batch-brbl-a-u02-b001.test.ts.

statement: Explain the purpose of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, its amendments, the Rules and the powers of the Director
source_caveats: The unit is the courseware account of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (as amended in 2012 and 2019) and of the Prevention of Money Laundering (Maintenance of Records of the Nature and Value of Transactions, the Procedure and Manner of Maintaining and Time for Furnishing Information and Verification and Maintenance of Records of the Identity of the Clients of the Banking Companies, Financial Institutions and Intermediaries) Rules, 2004 as amended up to 2013. No Act or Rules text was retrieved, so section numbers, thresholds, periods and penalties are taught only as the courseware states them and must be checked against the Act and Rules as amended to the 30 June 2026 cut-off (the Rules were amended after 2013, including on beneficial ownership and the reporting thresholds, and the Reserve Bank KYC Master Direction now governs bank due diligence) before publication.

Held back as not verified and not asked in any question: the individual convictions, sentences and fines in the four court cases the courseware summarises (Rose Valley, a Chennai importer, a drug related case and the case of a former State chief minister); the cases are taught only as illustrations of the offence and that the Special Court can convict, without figures.

The courseware describes the Director as an authority appointed by the Central Government and the reporting entity as including banking companies, financial institutions and intermediaries; the 2012 Amendment replaced the earlier terms with reporting entity; any later amendments to the definition are not checked.
The courseware describes the amount of the fine under Section 13(2) (not less than ten thousand rupees and up to one lakh rupees for each failure) as the 2012 text; later amendments are not checked.

The courseware text quotes a retention period of five years for transactions and identity records; this is the figure taught. The earlier unit of this paper (BRBL-A-U04-B001) noted a conflicting ten year statement in the courseware for Prevention of Money Laundering Act records; this unit contains no ten year statement.
